1 (Prioritized Buckets). Let B = (𝐵 0, 𝐵 1, . . . , 𝐵𝐿−1 ) denote an ordered sequence of buckets, where 𝐿 ∈ N is the number of levels. Bucket indices encode execution priority: buckets are accessed strictly in increasing index order (lower indices are considered earlier). By construction, 𝐵 0 coincides with the active bucket 𝐵 act , while 𝐵 ℓ for ℓ ≥ 1 are reserve buckets activated on demand when higher-priority buckets are exhausted. Data Structure for Prioritized Bucket. To generalize the reserve bucket 𝐵 res into a prioritized structure, we organize all paths into a multi-level buckets ordered by path weight. Specifically, each bucket layer corresponds to a progressively coarser weight interval, enabling the algorithm to localize updates within a small active subset while retaining global coverage over all candidates. In this way, selection correctness via a global ordering across buckets and enable provably safe early stopping during rebuilds to avoid redundant updates (Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3). Proc. ACM Manag. Suppose, for contradiction, that a rebuild is triggered while |𝐵 act | > 0 and some 𝜋𝑖 ∈ 𝐵 act has C𝑖 > 0. Let 𝜏 be the most recent admission threshold. By the maintenance invariants, 𝑊𝑖 ≤ 𝜏 for all 𝑖 ∈ 𝐵 act and 𝑊 𝑗 ≥ 𝜏 for all 𝑗 ∈ 𝐵 res . Thus a feasible in-bucket candidate satisfies 𝑊𝑖 ≤ 𝜏 ≤ 𝑊 𝑗 , so no reserve item can dominate it. Rebuilding is therefore unnecessary, leading to a contradiction. □

We prove by aggregate amortized analysis and decompose a bucket-rebuild epoch into three parts. (1) Bucket assignment and thresholding 𝑶 (| P|). We scan all |P | paths once to compute their current weights and assign each path to a reserve-bucket range. The top 𝐾 paths are then selected using a KLL-style quantile sketch [33], which returns the admission threshold 𝜏 and emits the top 𝐾 items. At most 𝐾 paths are inserted into the active bucket, and then these 𝐾 paths are inevitably consumed within the same epoch, either by being extracted as the current minimum or by being evicted after weight updates. (2) Building the active bucket 𝑶 (𝑲 log 𝑲 ). We insert up to 𝐾 paths into the active bucket, implemented as a binary-heap priority queue keyed by path weight. This costs 𝑂 (𝐾 log 𝐾). (3) Per-iteration maintenance 𝑶 (𝑻 log 𝑲 ). Across the 𝑇 selections in the epoch, each step performs an extract-min and triggers a constant number of localized heap updates and occasional insert operations on affected candidates. With a binary heap, each operation costs 𝑂 (log 𝐾); thus the 𝑂 (1) operations per selection accumulate to 𝑂 (𝑇 log 𝐾) time over the epoch. Suppose, for contradiction, there exist 𝑖 < 𝑖 ′ , a path 𝜋𝑝 ∈ 𝐵𝑖 , and a path 𝜋𝑞 ∈ 𝐵𝑖 ′ such that W(𝜋𝑞 ) < W(𝜋𝑝 ). By construction, buckets are formed from a global ordering of the paths by W(·), and are assigned in non-overlapping, index-ordered fashion so that all members of 𝐵𝑖 precede all members of 𝐵𝑖 ′ in that ordering. The strict inequality W(𝜋𝑞 ) < W(𝜋𝑝 ) implies that 𝜋𝑞 should appear before 𝜋𝑝 in the global order, hence 𝜋𝑞 must be placed in a bucket with index at most 𝑖, contradicting 𝜋𝑞 ∈ 𝐵𝑖 ′ with 𝑖 ′ > 𝑖. Therefore, our assumption is false and the claim follows. □

Assume, for contradiction, that the new global minimum weight 𝑤 ★ exceeds 𝜏𝑖 . At the previous rebuild, all paths in 𝐵𝑖 satisfied 𝑊 (𝜋) ≤ 𝜏𝑖 . Since at least one of them remains unaffected, its current weight is still ≤ 𝜏𝑖 , which contradicts the assumption that all paths now have 𝑊 (𝜋) > 𝜏𝑖 . Therefore, the new global minimum must satisfy 𝑤 ★ ≤ 𝜏𝑖 , and truncating the rebuild before 𝐵𝑖 does not miss the optimal path. □

The ranking of candidate paths is determined solely by their ordering key W(𝜋), which is independent of 𝐾. Changing 𝐾 alters only how many candidates are maintained per epoch, not their relative order. Each rebuild re-computes all relevant keys before the next iteration, ensuring that the same minimal path will be extracted regardless of 𝐾. Hence 𝐾 influences only computational efficiency, not the final or intermediate optimal path results. □
